# GitKraken Desktop Command Palette | Fast Actions & Navigation
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/command-palette/
Description: Discover how to use the Command Palette in GitKraken Desktop to quickly run commands, open files, switch repos, and customize settings with shortcuts.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Command Palette
Content type: how-to
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

<kbd>Last updated: April 2026</kbd>

Use this page to run GitKraken Desktop actions from the Command Palette when you want a keyboard-first workflow for commands, files, repositories, worktrees, and settings. It explains how to open the palette, what command categories are available, and when it is faster than navigating the UI directly.

**Requirements and limits**
- Access methods: <kbd>Cmd/Ctrl + P</kbd>, the wand icon, or the Help menu
- Scope: Commands, files, repositories, branches, stashes, worktree-related navigation, settings, logs, and patches
- Search behavior: Results filter live as you type
- Execution model: Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to run the selected item
- Command availability depends on the current repository state, open repo context, and configured integrations

<figure>
  <div class='embed-container embed-container--16-9'>
    <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/lNsQesvuRj4?rel=0&vq=hd1080" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>
  </div>
  <figcaption style="text-align:center; color:#888">Watch how to use the Command Palette for faster workflows.</figcaption>
</figure>

***

## Quick Start


- Open with <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> (macOS) or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> (Windows/Linux), or click the wand icon in the top-right toolbar.
- Start typing to filter available commands. Results update as you type.
- Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to run the selected command.

Common actions available through the Command Palette:
- **File management**: Create File, Delete File, Open File, Stage all changes, Discard all changes
- **Branch operations**: Create Branch, Rename Branch, Checkout, Push, Pull, Fetch All
- **Repository**: Open Repo, Clone, Init, Perform Repo Maintenance
- **Stash**: Create, Apply, Pop
- **View and settings**: Toggle Theme, Toggle Left Panel, Keyboard Shortcuts, Switch to Profile
- **Terminal and workflow**: Open in terminal for command-line tasks and manual coding agent workflows

The Command Palette is available at any time regardless of which panel or view is currently active in GitKraken Desktop.

***

## How to open the Command Palette

You can launch the Command Palette in three ways:

- Use the keyboard shortcut:
  - <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> on macOS
  - <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> on Windows/Linux
- Click the <i class="fa fa-magic" style="transform: rotate(225deg)"></i> icon in the top-right toolbar
- Go to the Help menu → <strong>Open Command Palette</strong>

<figure>
  <img src="/wp-content/uploads/command-palette-example.gif" class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Using the GitKraken Command Palette to filter and select commands, files, and branches, demonstrating how it accelerates navigation and common Git workflows without leaving the keyboard.">
  <figcaption style="text-align:center; color:#888">Start typing to filter commands, files, repos, and more.</figcaption>
</figure>

***

## What command categories are available

Below is a list of supported commands grouped by category.

### Repo
- `Close Tab`
- `Open Repo`
- `Open in file manager`
- `Open in External Editor`
- `Open in External Diff/Merge Tool`
- `Open in terminal`
- `Repo Management: Clone`
- `Repo Management: Init`
- `Repo Management: Open`
- `Perform Repo Maintenance`

`Open in terminal` is especially useful when you want to start a command-line workflow in the current repository or worktree, including a manual coding agent workflow. For more information, see [GitKraken Terminal Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/) and [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/).

### Settings
- `Configure Git Flow`
- `Configure LFS`
- `Configure GPG Signing`
- `Initialize LFS on this repo`
- `Join the Light side` / `Join the Dark side`
- `Manage Account`
- `Settings`
- `Switch to Profile` + `profile name`

### View
- `Decrease Zoom`
- `Increase Zoom`
- `Keyboard Shortcuts`
- `Reset Zoom`
- `Toggle Left Panel`
- `Toggle Commit Detail Panel`
- `Toggle Syntax Highlighting`
- `Toggle Theme`

### History
- `Blame` + `filename`
- `History` + `filename`
- `Search Commits` + `message` / `sha` / `author`

### Core
- `Redo`
- `Undo`

### File
- `Create File` + `filename`
- `Delete File` + `filename`
- `Open File` + `filename`
- `View File` + `filename`
- `Edit File` + `filename`
- `Discard all changes`
- `Stage all changes`
- `Unstage all changes`

### Stash
- `Stash: Apply`
- `Stash: Create`
- `Stash: Pop`

### Branch
- `Create Branch`
- `Create Tag`
- `Create Annotated Tag`
- `Fetch All`
- `Pull`
- `Push`
- `Rename Branch`
- `Start Pull Request`
- `View Working Directory Changes`

### Checkout
- `Checkout` + `{branch name}`

### Patch
- `Create patch from all working directory changes`
- `Apply patch`

### Logs
- `Activity logs`
- `View Error Logs`
- `View Performance Logs`
- `View Release Notes`

# GitKraken Desktop Documentation & Support | Master Git with GitKraken
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/gitkraken-desktop-home/
Description: Learn Git and run coding agents on their own branches with GitKraken Desktop. Find install guides, tutorials, integrations, release notes, and FAQs.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Help Center Home
Content type: home
Audience: all
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

GitKraken Desktop is a visual Git client for Windows, macOS, and Linux. You can use it for everyday Git work and to run coding agents on their own branches and worktrees, where their changes show up in the Commit Graph next to yours.

Start here to find installation steps, interface walkthroughs, coding agent workflows, worktrees, terminal usage, integrations, release notes, and support resources for GitKraken Desktop.

**Requirements and limits**
- Plan requirements, OS support, version limits, and step-by-step workflows are on each linked page.
- Installation, integrations, and release notes each list their own requirements and compatibility details.
- Coding agents, worktrees, the terminal, and on-premises deployment each have their own setup page.

Watch the overview video, or use the links below to go to the topic you need.

# GitKraken Desktop Interface Guide | Toolbar, Panels, and Graph
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/interface/
Description: Learn the GitKraken Desktop interface, including the toolbar, Left Panel, Commit Panel, and Commit Graph, where your work and coding agent work appear together.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Interface
Content type: overview
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-04

Use this page to find your way around the main areas of the GitKraken Desktop interface: the toolbar, Left Panel, Commit Graph, Commit Panel, Status Bar, and tabs. Each area links to a task guide when you need the full steps.

Use this page to find your way around the main areas of the GitKraken Desktop interface: the toolbar, Left Panel, Commit Graph, Commit Panel, Status Bar, and tabs. Each area links to a task guide when you need the full steps.

**Requirements and limits**
- Scope: Interface overview, not full task-specific workflows
- Main areas: Toolbar, Left Panel, Commit Graph, Commit Panel, Status Bar, and tabs
- Repository context: Most of these controls appear only when a repository is open
- Left Panel modes: The Left Panel shows either List view or the Agents view
- Left Panel behavior: You can show, hide, resize, collapse, or expand its sections
- Toolbar behavior: Some buttons, such as LFS, appear only when the relevant feature or repository state is available
- Zoom: The status bar zoom selector offers 80%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 120%, 130%, 140%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250%, and 300%. The View menu has **Increase Zoom**, **Decrease Zoom**, and **Reset Zoom**
- Detailed workflows: Follow the linked feature pages for the steps and limits of each task

***

## Quick Start

- **Left Panel**: Shows repository references, worktrees, and integrations. In `List | Agents`, click **List** for the traditional reference-based view or **Agents** for the Agents view, which organizes worktrees around coding agent sessions.
- **Commit Graph**: Displays the visual commit history of the current repository. Click any commit to view its details in the Commit Panel. Click the WIP node at the top to view and stage pending changes.
- **Commit Panel**: Shows file changes for the selected commit or WIP. Displays diffs, staged/unstaged files, and co-author information. Use it to stage files and write commit messages.
- **Toolbar**: At the top of the window. Has buttons for Undo, Redo, Pull, Push, Branch, Stash, and Pop. Use the adjacent dropdowns to customize pull behavior or branch options.
- **Status Bar**: At the bottom of the window. Shows the [Launchpad](/gitkraken-desktop/gitkraken-launchpad/) summary, your current plan, and a zoom selector with levels from 80% to 300%. You can also zoom from View > Increase Zoom, View > Decrease Zoom, and View > Reset Zoom, or with Cmd/Ctrl + =, Cmd/Ctrl + -, and Cmd/Ctrl + 0.

To open the Command Palette at any time, press Cmd/Ctrl + P. To toggle the Left Panel, use Cmd/Ctrl + J or the toggle in the toolbar. To open Preferences and integrations, click the gear icon in the upper-right corner.

***

From left to right, GitKraken Desktop displays the Left Panel, Commit Graph, and Commit Panel when working with a repository. The Left Panel can show either List view or the Agents view.

GitKraken Desktop UI includes Left Panel, Commit Graph, and Commit Panel.

## How the toolbar works

The main toolbar has buttons for common repository actions, including Undo, Redo, Pull, Push, and Branch.

### History actions

| Icon | Button | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-undo-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Undo** | The Undo button is active when you can undo an action. Click it to reverse the last undoable action. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-redo-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Redo** | Click Redo to reverse the last undo command. |

### Sync actions

| Icon | Button | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-pull-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Pull** | Click to pull changes from the remote repository. Use the adjacent dropdown to choose pull behavior: |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-push-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Push** | Push changes to the upstream remote repository. |

* Fetch All
* Pull (fast-forward if possible)
* Pull (fast-forward only): same as `git fetch && git merge --ff-only`
* Pull (rebase): same as `git fetch && git rebase`

Tip: Click the next to a pull type to make it the default. The selected default displays a .

### Branch actions

| Icon | Button | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-branch-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Branch** | Create a new branch from your current HEAD. |

### Work-in-progress actions

| Icon | Button | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-stash-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Stash** | Save your changes in a stash without committing them. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-pop-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Pop Stash** | Restore changes from the most recent stash. |

### Conditional actions

| Icon | Button | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-lfs-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **LFS** | This button appears if LFS is enabled for your repository. |

Note: To show labels under the toolbar icons, go to Preferences > UI Customization and enable Show toolbar icon labels.

***

## How the Left Panel works

The Left Panel shows repository references, such as local branches, remotes, and tags. You can:

* Collapse or expand sections
* Resize the panel and sections
* Show or hide sections from the context menu
* Maximize a section by double-clicking its header

To switch the Left Panel mode, use the `List | Agents` segmented control at the top of the panel:

* Click **List** for the traditional reference-based view described below.
* Click **Agents** to open the **Agents view**, which organizes the same worktrees around coding agent sessions, status, and quick actions. See [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/) for agent session setup and workflows.

To hide the segmented control, go to Preferences > UI Customization. For general worktree management, see [Manage Git Worktrees in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/worktrees/).

List view and the Agents view use the same underlying worktrees. Use List view for general branch and worktree management. Use the Agents view for coding agent sessions, agent status, and related quick actions.

For in-app terminal behavior, worktree-specific terminal sessions, and manual coding agent workflows, see [GitKraken Terminal Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/).

Resize, collapse, or expand any section of the Left Panel.

| Icon | Section | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-local-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Local** | References to local branches that point to specific commits.For help with branches, see Branching and Merging. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-remote-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Remote** | References to remote branches.For more information, see Pushing and Pulling. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-pull-requests-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Pull Requests** | Shows active pull requests for merging one branch into another.With a supported integration, you can create pull requests directly from GitKraken Desktop. For more information, see Pull Requests. |
|  | **Issues** | Shows issues connected to your repository integrations.For more information, see Jira, GitHub Issues, GitLab Issues, or Trello. |
|  | **Teams** | See what your Team members are working on. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-tags-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Tags** | References that point to specific commits and do not move.For more information, see Tags. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads/gk-new-stash-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Stashes** | Stored file changes from the working copy.For more information, see Stashing. |
| <img alt="" src='/wp-content/uploads//gk-new-submodules-icon.svg' class='img-responsive' style='width: 36px; height: 36px; object-fit: contain;'> | **Submodules** | A Git repository in a subdirectory of the current repository.For more information, see Submodules. |

### How to filter the Left Panel

Type in the Left Panel **Filter** box, or press Cmd/Ctrl + Option/Alt + F to focus it. The Left Panel shows only the items whose names match what you type. The match does not need to be exact, so you can type part of a name.

To find a branch on a specific remote, start the filter with the remote name, followed by `/` or `:`, such as `origin/main` or `origin:main`. GitKraken Desktop adds that remote's matching branches to the results.

***
## How the Commit Panel works

Use the Commit Panel to stage and commit files and changes from your working directory.

The Commit Panel displays file changes and commit metadata.

The Commit Panel has 3 sections, in the order you use them:

1. _Unstaged Files_ - Modified files not yet added to the index.
2. _Staged Files_ - Files staged for the next commit.
3. _Commit Message_ - A message in 2 parts:
   * **Summary**: A brief, informative message shown in the graph.
   * **Description**: Additional details to support the summary.

Color indicators help distinguish file changes (e.g., renamed, deleted).

For more about staging and committing, see [committing work](/working-with-commits/commits).

***

## How the Commit Graph works

Resize the Commit Graph by dragging column dividers.

The Commit Graph shows your repository's history as a graph of each commit and its relationships to other commits.

Each row is a commit, with the most recent at the top. Columns represent branches, and lines show merges and relationships.

Work from coding agents appears in the Commit Graph the same way. Each agent session runs on its own branch in its own worktree, with its own WIP node for pending changes. See [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/).

Legend for interpreting commit history and branching paths.

You can trace branch history from bottom to top and right to left.

### How ghost branches work

Hover over or select a commit to see its nearest containing branch ("ghost" branch). Double-click to check out its head.

Ghost branches help locate a commit’s closest reference.

### How commit highlighting works

Hovering over a branch highlights all related commits.

Unrelated commits fade when a branch is hovered.

To turn this behavior on or off, go to Preferences > UI Customization and select or clear **Highlight associated rows when hovering over a branch**.

***

## How tabs work

Switch between multiple repositories using tabs.

Rearrange tabs via drag-and-drop.

To switch tabs, press Cmd/Ctrl + 1 to 9. To open a new tab, click + or press Cmd/Ctrl + T. To close a tab, middle-click it or press Cmd/Ctrl + W.

Each [profile](/start-here/profiles/) keeps its own set of tabs.

Tabs adjust automatically when switching profiles.

Dropdown icon displays all open repositories.

Hover to view file paths associated with open tabs.

### Worktree tab groups

When you open 2 or more tabs from the same repository, such as the main repository and its [worktrees](/gitkraken-desktop/worktrees/), GitKraken Desktop groups them together in the tab bar. A group has a border around its tabs and a dotted handle on its left edge.

- Drag the handle to move the whole group.
- Right-click the handle and select **Close group** to close every tab in the group.
- Right-click a tab in the group and select **Close group** or **Close others in group**.
- In the tabs dropdown, grouped tabs appear indented under the repository name.

A group ends when fewer than 2 of its tabs are open. To stop grouping worktree tabs, go to Preferences > UI Customization and clear **Automatically group worktree tabs together**.

Tabs for a repository and its worktrees are grouped together.

### Tab alias and name

Right-click a tab and select Alias repository to assign a custom name.

Assign aliases to distinguish repositories in tabs.

***

## Columns

GitKraken Desktop displays these default columns: Branch/Tag, Graph, and Commit Message. You can rearrange the columns.

Drag column headers to reorder.

Right-click headers to toggle columns like Author, Date/Time, or Sha. You can also use the gear icon.

Enable/disable columns using header context menu.

Customize columns using the gear icon menu.

Filter commits by author via the  in the AUTHOR column.

Search and filter by commit author or team.

GitKraken Desktop saves column selections, widths, and order for each repository. You can also configure columns from Preferences > UI Customization.

For more advanced views, see [Hiding and Soloing](/working-with-repositories/hiding-and-soloing).

---

# GitKraken Desktop Keyboard Shortcuts | Speed Up Your Git Workflow
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/keyboard-shortcuts/
Description: Keyboard shortcuts for GitKraken Desktop on macOS, Windows, and Linux, for staging, committing, navigating the Commit Graph, and managing tabs and terminal tabs.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Keyboard Shortcuts
Content type: reference
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

Use these keyboard shortcuts to work in GitKraken Desktop on macOS, Windows, and Linux without leaving the keyboard. They cover staging, committing, navigating the Commit Graph, opening the Command Palette, managing tabs, toggling interface panels, and opening the terminal.

**Requirements and limits**
- Shortcuts differ between macOS and Windows/Linux, so check the column for your platform before using a shortcut.
- A shortcut works only when its view or repository is open.

<blockquote>Note: The &#8984; symbol refers to the Command key on macOS.</blockquote>

***

## How to open the keyboard shortcuts list

| Action | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open keyboard shortcuts | &#8984;/ | Ctrl/ |

## Keyboard shortcuts for repo actions
| Action | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create branch | &#8984;B | CtrlB |
| Fetch all | &#8984;L | CtrlL |
| Stage the current file | S | S |
| Stage all files | &#8984;ShiftS | CtrlShiftS |
| Unstage the current file | U | U |
| Unstage all files | &#8984;ShiftU | CtrlShiftU |
| Commit staged files with current message | &#8984;Enter | CtrlEnter |
| Stage all files and commit with current message | &#8984;ShiftEnter | CtrlShiftEnter |
| Focus commit message box | &#8984;ShiftM | CtrlShiftM |

### Keyboard shortcuts for navigation
| &nbsp; | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select previous item | K or &uarr; | K or &uarr; |
| Select next item | J or &darr; | J or &darr; |
| Select the item to the right | L or &rarr; | L or &rarr; |
| Select the item to the left | H or &larr; | H or &larr; |
| Select next item in branch | Shift&darr; ShiftJ | Shift&darr; ShiftJ |
| Select previous item in branch | Shift&uarr; ShiftK | Shift&uarr; ShiftK |
| Select first commit in graph | &#8984;&uarr; | CtrlHOME |
| Select last commit in graph | &#8984;&darr; | CtrlEND |
| Undo | &#8984;Z | CtrlZ |
| Redo | &#8984;Y &#8984;ShiftZ | CtrlY CtrlShiftZ |

### Keyboard shortcuts for the Command Palette
| &nbsp; | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Toggle Command Palette | &#8984;P | CtrlP |
| Search commits | &#8984;F | CtrlF |
| Open repo via Command Palette | &#8984;ShiftO | CtrlShiftO |
| Search file to view history and blame | &#8984;ShiftH | CtrlShiftH |
| Focus the Left Panel filter bar | &#8984;OptionF | CtrlAltF |
| Open current repo in default terminal | OptionT | AltT |
| Open current repo in File Manager | OptionO | AltO |
| Open diff or merge tool | &#8984;D | CtrlD |
| Close current repo | &#8984;W | CtrlW |
| Search within file (if file content has focus) | &#8984;F | CtrlF |

**Open current repo in default terminal** opens the current repository in your external terminal. To run commands or manual coding agent workflows in the in-app terminal for the current repository or worktree, see [GitKraken Terminal Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/).

### Keyboard shortcuts for the interface
| &nbsp; | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Toggle Full Screen | Control&#8984;F | F11 |
| Increase Zoom | &#8984;&equals; &#8984;&plus; | Ctrl&equals; Ctrl&plus; |
| Decrease Zoom | &#8984;&minus; | Ctrl&minus; |
| Reset Zoom | &#8984;0 | Ctrl0 |
| Toggle the Left Panel | &#8984;J | CtrlJ |
| Toggle the Commit Detail panel | &#8984;K | CtrlK |
| Focus the search bar | &#8984;F | CtrlF |
| Focus the Left Panel filter bar | &#8984;OptionF | CtrlAltF |
| Close the current panel (if one is open) | Esc | Esc |

### Keyboard shortcuts for tabs
| &nbsp; | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Tab | &#8984;T | CtrlT |
| Close Tab | &#8984;W | CtrlW |
| Switch to tab 1-9 | &#8984;#1-9 | Ctrl#1-9 |
| Jump to next open tab | ControlTab | CtrlTab |
| Jump to previous open tab | ControlShiftTab | CtrlShiftTab |
| Focus the repository search on a New Tab | &#8984;OptionF | CtrlAltF |

On a New Tab, the repository search box shows this shortcut in its placeholder text.

### Keyboard shortcuts for terminal tabs
| &nbsp; | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New terminal tab | &#8984;OptionN | CtrlShiftN |
| Close terminal tab | &#8984;OptionW | CtrlShiftW |
| Jump to the next terminal tab | &#8984;Option&rarr; | CtrlPage Down |
| Jump to the previous terminal tab | &#8984;Option&larr; | CtrlPage Up |
| Jump to terminal tab 1-9 | &#8984;Option#1-9 | CtrlShift#1-9 |

Terminal tab shortcuts work while the terminal panel is open. The same actions are in the View > Terminal Tabs menu on Windows and Linux, and in Window > Terminal Tabs on macOS. For more information, see [How terminal tabs work](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/#how-terminal-tabs-work).

---

# GitKraken Desktop Preferences | Customize Settings & Workflow
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/preferences/
Description: Find where each GitKraken Desktop setting lives in Preferences, including themes, integrations, profiles, commit signing, notifications, and terminal settings.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Preferences
Content type: reference
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-04

Use this page to understand what each major Preferences section controls in GitKraken Desktop, including profiles, integrations, AI settings, external tools, commit signing, terminal behavior, Agents view settings, and repository-specific options. Start here when you need to know where a setting lives before changing your workflow or environment.

**Requirements and limits**
- Scope: Preferences overview for app-wide, profile-specific, and repository-specific settings
- Access point: Gear icon in the top-right corner of GitKraken Desktop
- Profile behavior: Preferences are stored per profile, so switching profiles changes integrations and UI configuration
- Repo-specific settings: Some settings apply only to the currently open repository
- Plan-gated sections: Organization settings, GitKraken AI, and some notification controls depend on plan level
- Detailed workflows: Follow the linked feature pages for the steps and limits of each feature

***

## Quick Start

- **General**: Set auto-fetch intervals, conflict detection behavior, commit graph limits, and tab retention.
- **Profiles**: Create and switch between profiles to separate Git identities, integrations, and tab sets.
- **SSH and Integrations**: Connect to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Jira, Trello, and more.
- **GitKraken AI**: Enable AI-assisted commit messages and PR descriptions (Pro plan and above).
- **External Tools**: Set your preferred editor, diff tool, merge tool, external terminal, and custom coding agent commands.
- **UI Customization**: Change themes, date formats, avatar display, and commit graph metadata.
- **Commit Signing**: Enable GPG signing for verified commits.
- **Experimental**: Try preview features such as Git Executable and Cloud Patches.
- **Repo-Specific Preferences**: Configure encoding, Gitflow, hooks, LFS, issues, Team View, and agent setup commands per repository.

Preferences are stored per profile, so switching profiles resets integrations and UI options to that profile's configuration.

Access Preferences from the gear icon in the top right corner

***

## How organization settings work

This section is labeled with your organization's name. It shows members and teams, and allows Owners and Admins to:
- Manage member roles
- Invite users and assign licenses
- Create and manage teams

Note: Organization settings are available on the Pro plan and above.

***

## How General preferences work

Configure app-wide behavior like auto-fetch, conflict detection, and commit graph settings.

| Setting | What it controls |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto-Fetch Interval** | Sets the interval from 0 to 60 minutes. 0 disables auto-fetch. |
| **Auto-Prune** | Removes stale remote-tracking references. |
| **Enable proactive conflict detection with target branch** | GitKraken Desktop checks for conflicts with the base branch. |
| **Keep submodules up to date** | Updates submodules automatically after Git actions. |
| **Default Branch Name** | Sets the branch name for new repositories (default is `main`). |
| **Delete ".orig" files after merging** | Controls cleanup of merge backup files. |
| **Show All Commits in Graph** | Can affect performance on large repositories. |
| **Initial Commits in Graph** | Sets the number of commits the graph shows at first (minimum 500). |
| **Lazy Load Commits in Graph** | Loads more commits only as needed. |
| **Remember tabs** | Saves open tabs and profile context between sessions. |
| **Longpaths** and **AutoCRLF** | Windows-only settings tied to your global `.gitconfig`. |
| **Use extended logging in activity log** | Records more detailed activity logs, which you can get from Help > Support Logs. |
| **Forget all Usernames and Passwords** | Clears stored usernames and passwords. |
| **Share my current branch status with my team** | Shares your work in progress with teammates in [Team View](/gitkraken-desktop/team-view/). |

***

## How profile preferences work

Each profile keeps its own settings, tabs, and integrations, so you can keep separate setups when you work with more than one account.

See [how to create and switch profiles](/start-here/profiles).

***

## How SSH and integration preferences work

Control access and connections to remote repositories:

- [SSH settings](/gitkraken-desktop/authentication/#ssh)
- Git hosting integrations such as GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps
- Issue tracker integrations such as Jira and Trello

***

## How GitKraken AI preferences work

This feature is available for Pro plans or higher.

Use [GitKraken AI](/gitkraken-desktop/gkd-gitkraken-ai) to automate repetitive Git tasks.

The **Usage Details** card shows how many AI credits you have used this week and when your credits reset. Below it, the **Shared Organization Pool** meter shows your organization's credits this week, split into **Your usage**, **Rest of organization**, and **Remaining**.

When you reach your weekly credit limit, the card shows **You've reached your weekly credit limit**. GitKraken AI then draws from your organization's shared credit pool, so you can keep working. Every member of the organization can use the shared pool, and it resets weekly along with your personal limit.

- Organization Owners and Admins on a paid plan can click **Get more AI credits** to add credits.
- Users on a trial can click **Upgrade to get more credits**.

See the GitKraken AI FAQ for common questions.

***

## How external tool preferences work

Configure your preferred editors, terminals, coding agent commands, and diff/merge tools.

- **External Merge Tool**: [View supported tools](/working-with-repositories/branching-and-merging/#external-merge-tools)
- **External Diff Tool**: [View supported tools](/working-with-commits/diff/#external-diff-tools)
- **External Editor**: Choose from VS Code, Atom, Sublime, IntelliJ, or custom path
- **External Terminal**: The terminal that opens from File > Open External Terminal or Alt/Option + T. For a custom terminal, set **Terminal Executable** and **Terminal Arguments**
- **Coding Agent**: Configure custom commands or arguments used when GitKraken Desktop starts a coding agent session. GitKraken Desktop detects the supported coding agent CLIs installed on your machine, such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. You choose the coding agent for a session in the **Start an Agent Session** modal. In on-premises environments, available options depend on what your organization allows and can reach. See [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/).
- **Agent Status Integrations**: Install, reinstall, or uninstall the plugins that let Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, and OpenCode report live session status in the Agents view. See [How to manage agent status plugins and hooks](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/#how-to-manage-agent-status-plugins-and-hooks).

macOS Note: Use the executable file, not the .app, when selecting a custom editor.

***

## How notification preferences work

Control product and marketing messages:
- **Enable Desktop Notifications**
- **Receive Marketing Notifications**

Note: Only Pro, Advanced, Business, and Enterprise users can turn off marketing notifications.

***

## How UI customization preferences work

Change the theme and how the Commit Graph looks:
- [Themes](/start-here/themes)
- Notification location
- Date/time locale and formatting
- Author initials or avatars
- Graph metadata, such as branches, tags, author, commit message, and SHA
- **Hide Launchpad in status bar**
- **Show Agents view in left panel**. See [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/).
- **Automatically group worktree tabs together**: On by default. Groups the tabs of a repository and its worktrees in the tab bar. See [Worktree tab groups](/gitkraken-desktop/interface/#worktree-tab-groups).

If you want to switch between the standard Left Panel and the Agents view, go to Preferences > UI Customization and enable **Show Agents view in left panel**.

Enable Show Agents view in left panel to display the List | Agents toggle

***

## How commit signing preferences work

Enable and configure [GPG signing](/git-workflows-and-extensions/commit-signing-with-gpg/#configure-gpg-in-gitkraken) for commit verification.

***

## How editor preferences work

Customize code and diff viewer:
- Font, size, tab spacing
- EOL characters
- Syntax highlighting
- Line numbers and word wrap

***

## How in-app terminal preferences work

Adjust the appearance and behavior of the in-app terminal:
- Font, size, line height, cursor
- **Dim terminal when unfocused**: On by default. Fades the terminal output while you work elsewhere in the app
- Autocomplete behavior
- **Default In-App Terminal** on Windows

For worktree-specific terminal sessions and manual coding agent workflows, see [GitKraken Terminal Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/).

***

## How experimental preferences work

Preview [Experimental Features](/gitkraken-desktop/experimental-features):
- **Use Git Executable**: Run Git operations with a Git executable instead of the NodeGit library
- Cloud Patches

***

## How repo-specific preferences work

These settings apply only to the open repository, so you can configure each repository differently:

- [Encoding](/gitkraken-desktop/editing-files/#encoding)
- [Gitflow](/gitkraken-desktop/git-flow/)
- [Git Hooks](/gitkraken-desktop/githooks/)
- [LFS](/gitkraken-desktop/git-lfs/)
- [Commit settings](/working-with-commits/commits/)
- [Issues](/gitkraken-desktop/jira/)
- [Team View](/gitkraken-desktop/team-view/)
- [Submodules](/gitkraken-desktop/submodules/#keep-submodules-up-to-date)
- [Agents](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/#how-to-configure-setup-commands):
  - **Show worktree WIP nodes in the graph** (on by default) shows a WIP row in the Commit Graph for every other worktree with uncommitted changes or an active agent session
  - **Setup commands**, such as install scripts or build steps, run when a new agent session starts in a worktree

# GitKraken Desktop Tips | Productivity Shortcuts & Power Features
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/tips/
Description: GitKraken Desktop tips for Profiles, the Command Palette, keyboard shortcuts, coding agents, cherry pick, integrations, and the Commit Graph.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Tips and Power Features
Content type: overview
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

Use these tips to speed up everyday Git work in GitKraken Desktop. You can set up Profiles, navigate with the Command Palette and keyboard shortcuts, run coding agents in parallel worktrees, connect integrations, and control what the Commit Graph shows.

**Requirements and limits**
- Each tip is a summary. For full steps and edge cases, open the linked feature page.
- Some tips use paid features, including multiple Profiles and some integrations.
- Integration capabilities vary by Git provider and plan, especially for Azure DevOps and self-hosted services.
- Shortcuts, Command Palette actions, and other UI behavior can differ by operating system and by repository.

***

## How to set up profiles

Use [Profiles](/start-here/profiles) to keep work and personal repositories separate, or to manage multiple accounts.

Each profile can save a unique integration connection.

Each profile keeps its own Git config, preferences, and open tabs.

Note: Access to multiple profiles requires a GitKraken subscription.

***

## How to use the Command Palette

Use the [Command Palette](/start-here/command-palette) to find and run GitKraken Desktop actions from the keyboard.

Use the Command Palette to launch repositories, open editors, and more.

Common Command Palette actions include:

- **Undo** and **Redo**
- File actions: **Create File**, **Delete File**, **Open File**, **Edit File**, and **View File**
- Change actions: **Discard all changes**, **Stage all changes**, and **Unstage all changes**

***

## How to use keyboard shortcuts

Use [keyboard shortcuts](/start-here/keyboard-shortcuts) to run common actions without the mouse. To see the full list in GitKraken Desktop, use this shortcut:

| Action | Mac | Windows/Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open keyboard shortcuts | &#8984;/ | Ctrl/ |

***

## How to use the Agents view for parallel work

Use the Agents view to start and monitor coding agent sessions in parallel. In the Left Panel, use the `List | Agents` toggle to switch between List view and the Agents view. For setup and session steps, see [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/).

The Agents view uses the same underlying worktrees as List view, but organizes them around coding agent sessions, status, and quick actions. For general worktree management, see [Manage Git Worktrees in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/worktrees/).

***

## How to cherry pick multiple commits

Select multiple commits using Cmd/Ctrl or Shift, then right-click and select Cherry pick X commits.

Select multiple commits from the graph to cherry pick them together.

Before GitKraken Desktop applies the commits, you can reorder, squash, reword, or drop them. Learn more in [Interactive Cherry Pick](/gitkraken-desktop/cherrypick/).

***

## How to integrate with Git services

Connect GitKraken Desktop to [GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps](/gitkraken-desktop/integrations/) to work with your hosted repositories and pull requests.

Connect your Git provider to speed up repository access.

With an integration connected, you can:
- Create repositories and add a `.gitignore` or license file
- Clone from a list of your remote repositories
- Manage remotes and pull requests

Integration access depends on your plan:
- Community users can use public repositories on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket only.
- Azure DevOps integration requires a GitKraken subscription.
- Self-hosted services require a paid plan that supports self-hosted integrations.

***

## How to hide and solo branches

Control the Commit Graph display with [Hide and Solo](/gitkraken-desktop/hiding-and-soloing/) options.

    Hide branch icon.

    <h3>Hide</h3>
To hide a branch, click the eye  icon next to it in the Left Panel, or right-click it and select Hide. Hidden branches show a gray  icon.

    Solo branch icon.

    <h3>Solo</h3>
Right-click a branch and select Solo to show only that branch. Soloed branches show an orange  icon. To solo or unsolo other branches, click the solo icon next to each branch name in the Left Panel.

***

## How to view file history and blame

To [view file history and blame](/gitkraken-desktop/diff/#how-to-view-file-blame-and-history), click a commit and right-click a file.

Right-click a file to view its history or blame.

Switch between commit diff and file view with blame.

***

## How to open the GitKraken Desktop terminal

Run Git commands in the [GitKraken Terminal](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/). To open it, click the Terminal  button in the toolbar.

You can also use the embedded terminal to run coding agents by hand in a repository or worktree, including agents that GitKraken Desktop does not integrate with.

To choose the terminal that Alt/Opt + T opens, set a default terminal in Preferences > External Tools. For terminal sessions that follow your active worktree, see [GitKraken Terminal Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/).

***

## How to resize the Commit Graph

To resize the Commit Graph, hover over the graph's colored lines and drag.

Adjust the graph view to focus on the information you need.

# Install GitKraken Desktop on Windows, macOS & Linux | Setup Guide
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/how-to-install/
Description: Step-by-step installation guide for GitKraken Desktop on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Includes system requirements, video tutorials, and tips for WSL users.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Installation
Content type: how-to
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

<kbd>Last updated: April 2026</kbd>

This installation guide explains how to install GitKraken Desktop on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including platform-specific download methods, system requirements, and data locations. Use it when setting up GitKraken Desktop for the first time or when verifying the correct installer and OS support for your environment.

**Requirements and platform support**
- Windows: Windows 10+
- macOS: macOS 12+ on Intel and Apple Silicon
- Linux `.deb`: Ubuntu 18.04+ LTS or Debian 10+
- Linux `.rpm`: RHEL 8+ or Fedora 39+
- Linux support note: Other distributions may work but are not officially supported
- Advanced features note: Git command-line tools are optional for basic use, but recommended for features such as the terminal, experimental tools, or Git LFS
- Coding agent note: Coding agent CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode are installed separately from GitKraken Desktop

***

## Quick Start


1. [Download GitKraken Desktop](https://gitkraken.com/download?product=gitkraken&source=help_center) for your platform.
2. Run the installer:
   - **Windows**: Double-click the `.exe` file. GitKraken Desktop installs and launches automatically.
   - **macOS**: Open the `.dmg` file and drag the GitKraken icon into your Applications folder.
   - **Linux (.deb)**: Run `wget https://release.gitkraken.com/linux/gitkraken-amd64.deb && sudo apt install ./gitkraken-amd64.deb`.
   - **Linux (.rpm)**: Run `wget https://release.gitkraken.com/linux/gitkraken-amd64.rpm && sudo dnf install ./gitkraken-amd64.rpm`.
3. Launch GitKraken Desktop:
   - **Windows/macOS**: Use the shortcut or Applications folder.
   - **Linux**: Run `gitkraken` in a terminal.

No Git command-line tools are required for basic use. For advanced features like the terminal, Git LFS, or experimental tools, [install Git from git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/). If you want to use coding agents in GitKraken Desktop, install the coding agent CLI separately. For more information, see [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/).

***

## How to install GitKraken Desktop on each platform

There are three simple steps to get started with GitKraken Desktop:

1. [Download GitKraken Desktop](https://gitkraken.com/download?product=gitkraken&source=help_center)
2. Install GitKraken Desktop
3. Launch and start using GitKraken Desktop

No Git command-line tools are required. Once you run the installer, you can open the app and start working with your repositories.

If you want to use advanced features such as the terminal, experimental tools, or Git LFS, we recommend you [download Git from git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/). If you want to use coding agents, install the coding agent CLI separately from GitKraken Desktop.

Below are platform-specific installation instructions and system requirements.

<div class='callout callout--basic'>
    <p>Looking for <em>GitKraken On-Premise Self-Hosted</em> installation instructions? Please begin with our <a href="/enterprise/system-requirements">On-Premise System Requirements</a> page.</p>
</div>

---

## How to install GitKraken Desktop on Windows

**System requirements:** Windows 10+

- [Download GitKraken Desktop for Windows (64-bit)](https://gitkraken.com/download/windows64)

### How to run the Windows installer

Double-click the downloaded executable file. A splash screen will appear while GitKraken Desktop is installed. The application will automatically start when installation completes.

### Where GitKraken Desktop stores data on Windows

GitKraken Desktop data is stored in your user profile directory at:

```
C:\\Users\\{user}\\AppData\\Roaming\\.gitkraken
```

**System requirements:**
- Intel: macOS 12+
- Apple Silicon: macOS 12+

GitKraken Desktop data is stored in:

/Users/{user}/.gitkraken
```

or using the shorthand:

```

## How to install GitKraken Desktop on Linux

**System requirements:**
- **.deb**: Ubuntu 18.04+ LTS or Debian 10+
- **.rpm**: RHEL 8+ or Fedora 39+

<div class='callout callout--warning'>
    <p>Note 📝 - GitKraken Desktop officially supports Ubuntu 18.04+ LTS, RHEL 8+, and Fedora 39+. While it may run on other distributions, compatibility is not guaranteed.</p>
</div>

<div class='embed-container embed-container--16-9'>
    <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Cx4aQzlMSw4?ecver=1" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</div>

### How to install the .deb package
In your terminal, run:
```bash
wget https://release.gitkraken.com/linux/gitkraken-amd64.deb
sudo apt install ./gitkraken-amd64.deb
```
Or [download the .deb installation package](https://gitkraken.com/download/linux-deb?product=gitkraken&source=help_center).

### How to install the .rpm package
```bash
wget https://release.gitkraken.com/linux/gitkraken-amd64.rpm
sudo dnf install ./gitkraken-amd64.rpm
```
Or [download the .rpm installation package](https://gitkraken.com/download/linux-rpm?product=gitkraken&source=help_center).

> For older distributions without `dnf`, use `yum` instead.

### How to install the .tar.gz archive
```bash
wget https://release.gitkraken.com/linux/gitkraken-amd64.tar.gz
sudo tar -xvzf gitkraken-amd64.tar.gz
```
Or [download the .tar.gz archive](https://gitkraken.com/download/linux-gzip?product=gitkraken&source=help_center).

### How to install from Snap

Install GitKraken from [Snapcraft.io](https://snapcraft.io/gitkraken?product=gitkraken&source=help_center).

### Where GitKraken Desktop stores data on Linux

GitKraken Desktop data is stored in:

```
/home/{user}/.gitkraken
```

or

```
~/.gitkraken
```

### How to use GitKraken Desktop with WSL

To use GitKraken Desktop with Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), refer to [our WSL setup guide](https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/windows-subsystem-for-linux/).

---

## How to launch GitKraken Desktop after installation

Once installed, launch GitKraken Desktop as follows:

- **Windows:** Use the Start Menu shortcut or search for GitKraken.
- **macOS:** Open the Applications folder and double-click GitKraken.
- **Linux:** Open a terminal and run:

```bash
gitkraken
```

You’re now ready to start using GitKraken! For help getting started with repositories, branches, and remotes, check out the [Getting Started Guide](https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-client/introduction-to-gitkraken-client/).

# Learn Git with GitKraken Desktop | Beginner Guide & Workflow
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/guide/
Description: New to Git? Get started with GitKraken Desktop using this beginner-friendly guide. Learn cloning, branching, staging, committing, and merging with tutorials and videos.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Beginner Guide
Content type: how-to
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

Learn a basic GitKraken Desktop workflow: clone a repository, create a branch, make and stage changes, commit them, push the branch, and merge the work back. These steps are for new Git users who want a practical first path through GitKraken Desktop.

Learn a basic GitKraken Desktop workflow: clone a repository, create a branch, make and stage changes, commit them, push the branch, and merge the work back. These steps are for new Git users who want a practical first path through GitKraken Desktop.

**Requirements and limits**
- The steps cover a basic workflow, not every GitKraken Desktop option or edge case.
- You need access to a Git repository you can clone, change, commit to, and push from GitKraken Desktop.
- Whether you can push and merge depends on your remote permissions and repository policy.
- Resolving merge conflicts is outside these steps. See [Branching and Merging](/working-with-repositories/branching-and-merging).

***

## Quick Start

1. **Clone a repository**: Go to File > Clone Repo, paste a repository URL or browse your connected Git hosting service, and click **Clone the repo!**.
2. **Create a branch**: Right-click any commit in the graph and select **Create branch here**. Name it and press Enter.
3. **Make changes**: Edit files in your working directory. Saved changes appear under the WIP node in the Commit Graph.
4. **Stage changes**: Click the WIP node to open the Commit Panel. Click files to stage them, or press Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + S to stage all.
5. **Commit**: Enter a commit message and press Cmd + Enter (macOS) or Ctrl + Enter (Windows/Linux).
6. **Push**: Click **Push** in the toolbar to upload your branch to the remote.
7. **Merge**: When your work is ready, check out the target branch, right-click your feature branch, and select **Merge *[feature branch]* into *[target branch]***.

If the merge has conflicts, GitKraken Desktop opens the Merge Tool, where you can select lines from each side and commit the resolution.

***

## How to learn Git with GitKraken

This video series teaches Git concepts and how to apply them in GitKraken Desktop.

Git tutorial series for beginners.

To see how version control fits into a DevOps workflow, read the GitKraken [DevOps Tools Report](https://www.gitkraken.com/resources/devops-report-2020).

***

## GitKraken tutorials

Watch these video tutorials to learn the GitKraken Desktop interface.

Video tutorials for using GitKraken Desktop.

***

## How local repositories work

Most Git actions in GitKraken Desktop run in your local repository, on your machine. In the Commit Graph, the  icon marks local branches.

Git is fast because it makes changes locally, not over a network. If a remote server fails, each copy of the repository on your team still has the full project history.

### What the `.git` folder does

The `.git` folder holds your repository's metadata and commit history. If you delete it, Git operations such as switching branches or pulling from remotes do not work.

### What the working directory does

The working directory holds the files you are working on. When you switch branches or pull updates, Git changes the files in your working directory to match the checked-out branch.

Learn more about [Git repositories](https://www.gitkraken.com/learn/git/tutorials/what-is-a-git-repository).

***

## How the example workflow works

Follow this workflow to make your first commit in GitKraken Desktop.

### How to create a branch

Right-click `main` in the Commit Graph and choose Create branch here. Name it `develop`, a branch for ongoing development.

Right-click main to create a new branch.

### How to modify a file

Edit `README.md` to reflect your project. You can open this file directly from the Commit Graph.

Click a filename to access the Edit button.

### How to stage and commit changes

After editing, select the //WIP node to view unstaged changes. To stage all of them, click the green <button class='button button--success button--ui button--nolink'>Stage All Changes</button> button.

Click the WIP node to view and stage changes.

Then enter a commit message and click <button class='button button--success button--ui button--nolink'>Commit Changes to 1 File</button>.

Learn more about [staging](/working-with-commits/staging) and [committing](/working-with-commits/commits).

### How to merge back to main

When `develop` is ahead of `main`, you can merge:

Develop is ahead by 1 commit.

To merge, drag `develop` onto `main` in the Commit Graph and select Merge develop into main.

Drag develop onto main to merge branches.

Learn more in [Branching and Merging](/working-with-repositories/branching-and-merging).

***

## Getting started summary

This basic workflow sets the foundation for more advanced topics like [pushing and pulling](/working-with-repositories/pushing-and-pulling) and [GitFlow](/git-workflows-and-extensions/git-flow).

When you are ready to go further, continue with:

- [GitKraken Desktop Interface Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/interface/) to learn how the Left Panel, Commit Graph, and Commit Panel fit together
- [Manage Git Worktrees in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/worktrees/) to work on multiple branches in parallel
- [GitKraken Terminal Guide](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/) to use the embedded terminal
- [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/) to use the Agents view and coding agent workflows

Watch how to make a commit in GitKraken Desktop:

Walkthrough of creating a commit in GitKraken Desktop.

# Open, Clone, or Initialize a Git Repository in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/open-clone-init/
Description: Learn how to open, clone, or initialize repositories in GitKraken Desktop. Get started with repository management and project setup.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Repository Management
Content type: how-to
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

Use this page to open an existing local repository, clone a remote repository, or initialize a new repository in GitKraken Desktop. You can also use shallow clone, sparse checkout, and the Repository Management tab to set up a new or existing project.

**Requirements and limits**
- Entry points: Repository Management tab, New Tab, File &gt; Clone Repo / Init Repo / Open Repo, or the `gitkraken` command line
- Open workflow: Requires an existing local Git repository
- Clone workflow: Requires a remote repository URL or a connected integration
- Shallow clone: Supports branch, depth, since-date, and custom clone flags
- Sparse checkout: Root-level files are always checked out even when path rules are applied
- Initialize workflow: Creates a `.git` directory and can optionally add a `README.md`, `.gitignore`, and `LICENSE`
- Command line: You can open a repository by passing its path as an argument (for example, `gitkraken .` or `gitkraken /path/to/repo`) without the `--path` flag

***

## Quick Start

**To open an existing local repository:**
1. Click the folder icon in the top-left corner or press Alt + O (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + O (Mac).
2. Click **Browse** and select your repository folder.

**To open a repository from the command line:**
Pass the repository path directly as an argument, for example `gitkraken .` to open the current directory or `gitkraken /path/to/repo` to open a specific path. You do not need the `--path` flag.

**To clone a remote repository:**
1. Open the Repository Management tab and click **Clone**.
2. Enter the repository URL or select a repository from your connected integration.
3. Click **Clone the repo!** to download it locally.

**To initialize a new repository:**
1. Click **Init** in the Repository Management tab.
2. Fill in the repository path and optional settings (`.gitignore`, license).
3. Click **Create Repository** to create the repo and open it.

To limit commit history by depth or date when you clone, enable **Shallow Clone** in the Clone dialog. You can open, clone, and initialize repositories from the Repository Management tab, the New Tab, or File > Clone Repo / Init Repo / Open Repo.

***
## How to complete the initial setup
Complete these setup steps before managing repositories:

1. [Install GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/how-to-install)
2. Create an account and configure your [profile](/gitkraken-desktop/profiles). GitKraken Desktop opens your browser to sign up or sign in at gitkraken.dev. If you choose a provider such as GitHub during setup, gitkraken.dev opens with that provider selected.

***
## How Repository Management works

The **Repository Management** tab shows your active repositories, Workspaces, and favorites. Open this tab by clicking the folder icon in the top-left or using:
- Alt + O (Windows/Linux)
- Cmd + O (Mac)

Repository Management tab in GitKraken Desktop

From here, you can:
- **Browse**: Open a local Git repository.
- **Clone**: Copy a remote Git repository to your machine.
- **Init**: Initialize a new Git repository or reinitialize an existing one.

This tab also includes Workspaces and repository actions:
- Open in VS Code
- View repository details (README.md panel)
- Open/Close repo tab

***
### How to open an existing project

To open an existing repo:

1. From Repository Management, select <button class='button button--primary button--ui button--nolink'>Browse</button>.
2. Use the file explorer to locate your repo.

Select an existing repository to open

You can also browse for a repository from the New Tab, which you open with the + icon.

#### How to open a repository from the command line

You can open a repository in GitKraken Desktop by running the `gitkraken` command and passing the repository path directly as an argument:

```bash
# Open the current directory
gitkraken .

# Open a specific repository path
gitkraken /path/to/repo
```

The `--path` flag is not required.

#### How to open shallow-cloned repositories

GitKraken Desktop opens shallow-cloned repositories with no special setup. Open the shallow clone’s folder as you would any other repository.

***
### How to clone a project

To clone a remote repo:

1. In Repository Management, select <button class='button button--primary button--ui button--nolink'>Clone</button>.

Clone from Repository Management tab

2. Enter the clone URL, or select a repository from a connected integration. You can also open the clone options from File > Clone Repo or the New Tab.

Enter the clone URL to start

#### How shallow clone works

GitKraken Desktop supports **shallow cloning** when cloning a repository. Shallow clones let you limit the commit history that is downloaded, which can reduce clone time and disk usage for large repositories.

To perform a shallow clone:

1. Open the **Clone** dialog from **Repository Management**, the **New Tab**, or File > Clone Repo.
2. Select the repository you want to clone.
3. Enable the **Shallow Clone** option.

Shallow Clone option in the Clone dialog

Selecting **Shallow Clone** shows these options:

- **Branch to clone**: Specify the branch to clone. By default, GitKraken Desktop uses the repository’s default branch.
- **Depth**: Set how many commits deep to clone from the selected branch.
- **Since date**: Limit the clone to commits newer than a specific date.
- **Custom flags**: Provide any additional flags you typically pass to the `git clone` command. Enter these exactly as you would in the command-line interface.

4. Click <button class='button button--success button--ui button--nolink'>Clone the repo!</button> to complete the shallow clone.

After cloning, the repository opens automatically in GitKraken Desktop.

#### How sparse checkout works

Sparse checkout lets you check out only a subset of files from a repository, keeping your working directory smaller and improving performance on large repositories such as monorepos.

To perform a sparse checkout when cloning:

1. Open the **Clone** dialog from **Repository Management**, the **New Tab**, or File > Clone Repo.
2. Select the repository you want to clone.
3. Enable the **Sparse Checkout** option.
4. In the **Paths to include** field, enter one path per line (for example, `src/`, `docs/`, `README.md`). If you enter no paths, GitKraken Desktop checks out only root-level files.

Enable Sparse Checkout in the Clone dialog and specify which paths to include.

5. Click <button class='button button--success button--ui button--nolink'>Clone the repo!</button> to complete the clone.

Note: Files at the root of the repository are always checked out regardless of the paths you specify.

#### How to configure sparse checkout on an existing repository

To enable or update sparse checkout rules on a repository you have already opened, go to Preferences > Sparse Checkout for that repository.

Configure sparse checkout paths and actions under Repo-Specific Preferences.

From this panel you can:
- **Enable sparse checkout**: Turns on sparse checkout with the paths you have entered.
- **Disable sparse checkout**: Turns off sparse checkout and restores the full working directory.
- **Reapply sparse checkout**: Reapplies the current path rules. Use it after you pull in new files or resolve inconsistencies.

When a repository has sparse checkout active, a **Sparse** button appears in the toolbar. Click it to edit your sparse checkout paths, disable sparse checkout, or reapply the current rules without opening Preferences.

The Sparse toolbar button provides quick access to sparse checkout commands on active repos.

***
### How to initialize a new project

To start a new repo:

1. Select <button class='button button--primary button--ui button--nolink'>Init</button> in Repository Management.

Repository initialization options

2. Fill in:
   - Repository path
   - `.gitignore` template (optional)
   - License (optional)

3. Click <button class='button button--success button--ui button--nolink'>Create Repository</button>.

You can also initialize a repository from File > Init Repo or the New Tab.

After initialization:
- GitKraken Desktop creates a `.git` directory.
- The repository opens in GitKraken Desktop.
- The repository includes `README.md`, and optionally `.gitignore` and `LICENSE`.

You can also initialize a repository directly to GitHub, Bitbucket, or other remote providers.

***
### How to customize Repository Management

You can customize the Repository Management tab:
- Drag group headers to reorder them.
- To change a group's color, select Change color in the repo group menu.
- To set default colors, go to Preferences > UI Customization.

Customize repo group layout and colors

---

# Add, Delete, and Filter Files in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/adding-and-removing/
Description: Learn how to create, delete, and manage files and folders in GitKraken Desktop using the Command Palette, context menu, and file filter. This page covers file and folder operations only — for adding or removing remotes, see the Remotes documentation.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: File Management
Content type: how-to
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

<kbd>Last updated: March 2026</kbd>

<div class="callout callout--note">
<p><strong>Note:</strong> This page covers creating, deleting, and filtering files inside a repository. To add or remove a remote repository, see <a href="/gitkraken-desktop/pushing-and-pulling/">Remote Repositories and Pushing/Pulling</a>.</p>
</div>

Use this page to create files, create folders, delete files, and filter repository contents from inside GitKraken Desktop. It covers both Command Palette and context-menu workflows, plus the `View all files` mode you need when you want to delete or locate files outside the current staged or changed set.

**Requirements and limits**
- Workflow scope: File and folder creation, deletion, and filtering inside an existing repository
- Create-file access: Command Palette or Commit Panel context menu
- Folder creation behavior: Include `/` in the new filename to create a folder and file at the same time
- Delete-file limitation: To delete arbitrary repository files, enable `View all files` first
- Filter behavior: The `Filter Files` bar appears only when `View all files` is enabled

***

## Quick Start


**To create a file:**
1. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> to open the Command Palette.
2. Type `Create File` and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
3. Enter a filename and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. To create a folder at the same time, include a `/` in the name (e.g., `src/utils.js`).

**To create a file using the context menu:**
1. Right-click the empty space in the Commit Panel.
2. Select `Create File`.

**To delete a file:**
1. Right-click the file in the Commit Panel.
2. Select `Delete file`.

To delete any file in the repository (not just staged files), first enable `View all files` in the Commit Panel. Once enabled, right-click any file and select `Delete file`. A **Filter Files** bar also appears when `View all files` is on, letting you type a filename or extension to locate files quickly.

***

## How to add a file using the Command Palette

1. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd> to open the Command Palette.
2. Type `Create File` and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">Create a new file from the Command Palette.</figcaption>
</figure>

3. Type the desired filename and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/create-file-2025-gif.gif' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Using GitKraken Desktop's Command Palette to create and name a new file, demonstrating how developers can generate project files without leaving the keyboard or switching UI contexts.">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">Watch how to name and create a file.</figcaption>
</figure>

To create a folder and a file at once, include a forward slash (/) in the file name:

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/create-folder@2x.png' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Creating a new folder by including a slash in the file name, demonstrating how GitKraken Desktop auto-generates nested directory structures during file creation.">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">This creates a folder called &quot;folder-name&quot; that contains &quot;file-name.txt.&quot;</figcaption>
</figure>

***

## How to add a file using the context menu

You can also add files via the Commit Panel:

1. Right-click the empty space in the Commit Panel.
2. Select `Create File` from the context menu.

2. Select `Delete file` from the context menu.

2. Right-click the file you want to remove.

</figure>

***

When `View all files` is enabled, a <kbd>Filter Files</kbd> bar appears.
