# Detached HEAD in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/detached-head-state/
Description: Learn how to safely enter, work in, and exit detached HEAD state in GitKraken Desktop. Includes recovery tips and commit preservation.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Detached HEAD
Content type: how-to
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

<kbd>Last updated: March 2026</kbd>

Use this page to enter, work in, and recover from detached HEAD state in GitKraken Desktop when you need to inspect or test a specific commit without switching a branch pointer. It explains how to preserve commits created in detached HEAD state and how to recover lost work if you switch branches too early.

**Requirements and limits**
- Entry point: Check out a specific commit instead of a branch
- HEAD behavior: The checked-out commit is labeled `HEAD`
- Commit-preservation rule: Commits made in detached HEAD state are not attached to any branch until you create one
- Exit behavior: Checking out another branch removes the detached `HEAD` state
- Recovery options: Use GitKraken Desktop Undo if available, or use `git reflog` from the terminal to recover lost commit SHAs
- Risk: Unpreserved commits can be lost from normal branch history when you switch branches

***

## Quick Start


**To enter detached HEAD state:**
1. Right-click any commit in the Commit Graph.
2. Select **Checkout this commit**. The commit will display a `HEAD` label.

**To preserve commits made in detached HEAD state:**
1. Right-click the commit labeled `HEAD`.
2. Select **Create branch here** and name the new branch.

**To exit detached HEAD state:**
- Double-click any local branch in the graph or Left Panel to check it out.

Any commits made in detached HEAD state that were not saved to a branch will be removed when you switch branches. If you switch branches before creating a branch, use the **Undo** button if available, or run `git reflog` in the terminal to find the lost commit SHA and re-check it out with `git checkout <SHA>`.

***

## How to enter detached HEAD state

1. Right-click the commit you want to inspect.
2. Select <kbd><strong>Checkout this commit</strong></kbd>.

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/checkout-commit-2025.png' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Context menu showing 'Checkout this commit' option in GitKraken Desktop after right-clicking a specific commit in the graph view">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">Check out any past commit without creating a new branch.</figcaption>
</figure>

The checked-out commit will display a `HEAD` label, indicating you’re in detached HEAD state.

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/HEAD-2025.png' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="GitKraken Desktop showing HEAD label attached to a specific commit in the graph, indicating the currently checked-out commit">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">GitKraken tags the commit with HEAD.</figcaption>
</figure>

You can now review the full history and diffs, or create a branch from this state.

***

## How to commit in detached HEAD state

You can make changes and commit them while in this state. However, these commits won’t belong to any branch.

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/editing-detachedly-2025.png' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="GitKraken Desktop interface showing a warning banner that says 'You are in a detached HEAD state' above the commit panel with unstaged changes listed">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">GitKraken shows a warning when you commit in detached HEAD state.</figcaption>
</figure>

To preserve your work, create a branch from the current commit:

1. Right-click the commit tagged as HEAD.
2. Select <kbd><strong>Create branch here</strong></kbd>.

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/create-branch-from-HEAD-2025.png' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Context menu in GitKraken Desktop showing the option 'Create branch here' when right-clicking a commit labeled HEAD">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">Start a branch from your current detached commit to keep your changes.</figcaption>
</figure>

***

## How to exit detached HEAD state

To exit detached HEAD state:

- Check out any local branch.

This will remove the `HEAD` label and discard any unpreserved commits.

<figure class='figure center'>
  <img src='/wp-content/uploads/discard-commits.gif' class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Animation showing how unbranched commits in GitKraken Desktop are removed from view after switching branches from a detached HEAD state">
  <figcaption style="text-align: center; color: #888;">Unbranched commits are removed when you check out another branch.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class='callout callout--danger'>
  <p><strong>Important:</strong> Commits made in detached HEAD state will be lost unless you create a branch. You may be able to <a href='https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/detached-head-state/#recovering-lost-commits'>recover them manually</a>.</p>
</div>

***

## How to recover lost commits

If you accidentally switch branches before saving your changes:

- Click <a href="https://support.gitkraken.com/working-with-commits/undo-and-redo/">Undo</a> in GitKraken if available.
- Use the CLI and run [`git reflog`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-reflog) to find the lost commit SHA.
- Then use [`git checkout <SHA>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout) to re-enter that state.

---

# Pull Request Filter Syntax in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/pull-requests-filter-syntax/
Description: Use advanced filter syntax in GitKraken Desktop to find pull requests by title, author, label, branch, CI status, and more across supported integrations.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Pull Request Filter Syntax
Content type: reference
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

<kbd>Last updated: March 2026</kbd>

This reference explains how to filter pull requests in GitKraken Desktop by title, author, assignee, branch, status, and other supported fields. Use it when you need to narrow large pull request lists quickly or want to know which filter operators work for GitHub and other hosted integrations.

***

## Pull request filters supported for GitHub

### How to search by title or description

| Filter            | Example               | Description                                                        |
|------------------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Title/body search| `foo`                 | Matches PRs with `foo` in the title or description                |
| Exact match      | `foo bar`             | Matches PRs with `foo bar` in the title or description            |
| `in:` title only | `foo in:title`        | Matches PRs with `foo` in the title only                          |
| `in:` body only  | `foo in:body`         | Matches PRs with `foo` in the body only                           |

### How to filter by people

| Filter             | Example               | Description                                                      |
|-------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `author:`          | `author:keanu`        | PRs created by user `keanu`                                     |
| `assignee:`        | `assignee:keanu`      | PRs assigned to `keanu`                                         |
| `review-requested:`| `review-requested:jerry` | PRs needing review from `jerry`                             |
| `reviewed-by:`     | `reviewed-by:keanu`   | PRs already reviewed by `keanu`                                 |
| `involves:`        | `involves:jerry`      | PRs involving `jerry` via comment, review, or assignment        |

### How to filter by branch

| Filter     | Example            | Description                        |
|------------|--------------------|------------------------------------|
| `base:`    | `base:main`        | PRs targeting the `main` branch    |
| `head:`    | `head:development` | PRs from `development` branch      |

### How to filter by state and metadata

| Filter        | Example                | Description                                     |
|---------------|------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| `draft:`      | `draft:true`           | Draft PRs only                                 |
| `label:`      | `label:"Release Critical"` | PRs with the specified label             |
| `milestone:`  | `milestone:v1`         | PRs assigned to `v1` milestone                 |

### How to filter by review status

| Filter  | Example                 | Description                                       |
|---------|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `review:`| `review:approved`      | PRs approved by at least one reviewer             |
|         | `review:changes_requested`| PRs with change requests                        |
|         | `review:none`           | PRs without any reviews                           |

### How to filter by CI status

| Filter    | Example          | Description                        |
|-----------|------------------|------------------------------------|
| `status:` | `status:success` | PRs with successful CI             |
|           | `status:pending` | PRs with pending CI                |
|           | `status:failure` | PRs with failed CI                 |

### How to filter for missing values

| Filter | Example         | Description                      |
|--------|-----------------|----------------------------------|
| `no:`  | `no:assignee`   | PRs without an assignee          |
|        | `no:status`     | PRs without a CI status          |

### How to filter by date

| Filter     | Example                  | Description                          |
|------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| `created:` | `created:2020-12-31`     | PRs created on or after this date    |
| `updated:` | `updated:2020-12-31`     | PRs updated on or after this date    |

### How to combine or exclude filters

You can combine filters using commas (OR logic) or use a dash (`-`) to exclude.

**Examples:**
- `label:Bug,Feature` – PRs with either label
- `-assignee:guy` – PRs not assigned to `guy`
- `label:Bug,Feature label:Important` – PRs with Bug or Feature, and also Important

***

## Pull request filters supported for other integrations

GitKraken Desktop supports some—but not all—filter options across integrations:

| Integration           | updated: | review-requested: | assignee: | title/body/in/no/created/base/head | reviewed-by, review, involves, label, milestone, draft, status |
|------------------------|:--------:|:------------------:|:---------:|:----------------------------------:|:-------------------------------------------------------------:|
| GitLab / Self-Managed | ✔        |                    | ✔        | ✔                                  |                                                               |
| Bitbucket             | ✔        |                    | ✔        | ✔                                  |                                                               |
| Bitbucket Data Center | ✔        | ✔                  |          | ✔                                  |                                                               |
| Azure DevOps          |          |                    | ✔        | ✔                                  |                                                               |

<div class='callout callout--basic'>
  <p><strong>Tip:</strong> Use filters in the pull request panel to narrow down by author, label, or merge target.</p>
</div>

---

# Clean Up AI Coding Agent Commits Before Review in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/clean-up-agent-commits/
Description: Turn an AI coding agent's one giant commit, or a run of commits made in the order it worked, into a clean history a reviewer can follow, using Commit Composer in GitKraken Desktop.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Pull Request Filter Syntax
Content type: reference
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

Use this page when an AI coding agent leaves you with one giant commit, or with a run of small commits in the order it worked rather than grouped by change, and you need a history a reviewer can follow. Commit Composer in GitKraken Desktop groups the agent's changes into logical commits with clear messages. It only reorganizes the changes and never changes the code itself. You review and adjust the result before anything on your branch changes.

**Requirements and limits**
- Scope: Regrouping an agent's uncommitted changes or existing commits into a reviewable history before you open a pull request
- Prerequisite: A [paid GitKraken subscription](https://www.gitkraken.com/pricing?source=help_center&product=gitkraken) with GitKraken AI enabled. On-premises deployments need a custom AI endpoint (see [GitKraken AI](/gitkraken-desktop/gkd-gitkraken-ai/)).
- AI usage: Commit Composer uses your GitKraken AI credits, or your own AI provider if you set one up.
- Limits: Commit Composer is in Preview.
- Limits: To recompose existing commits, they must be contiguous, on the current branch, and have no merge commits between the branch head and the oldest selected commit.
- Limits: Recomposing commits you already pushed rewrites shared history.

***

## Quick Start

Before you start, open the agent's worktree: in the Agents view, right-click the session card and select **Open this worktree**. Then pick the row that matches what the agent left you.

| Where the changes are | What to use | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uncommitted, in the agent's worktree | **Compose commits with AI** | Stage the changes, then click **Compose commits with AI** in the Commit Panel | |
| Committed on the agent's branch, not pushed | **Recompose commits with AI** | Shift + click the agent's first and last commits, right-click, and select **Recompose *[number]* commits with AI (Preview)** | The commits must be next to each other, with no merge commits in between |
| Committed and pushed | **Recompose commits with AI**, then force push | Recompose as above, then force push the branch | Only if nobody else has pulled or built on the branch |

In every case, GitKraken Desktop shows the proposed commits first. Your branch does not change until you click **Create Commits**.

***

## Which AI credits Commit Composer uses

Commit Composer runs on GitKraken AI. By default, it uses your GitKraken AI credits. If you add your own provider and API key, such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Google Gemini, or a custom URL, Commit Composer uses that provider instead.

You can choose which set of credits a cleanup spends. For example, if your agent work is already running through one provider, you can compose commits with the other. To set your provider, go to Preferences  GitKraken AI. See [How to use your own AI provider key](/gitkraken-desktop/gkd-gitkraken-ai/) for setup.

***

## How to split an agent's uncommitted changes into commits

Use this when the agent changed files but did not commit anything.

1. Open the agent's worktree, then select its WIP node and stage the changes you want to commit. Selecting the agent's WIP row from another worktree does not open its files in the Commit Panel. Click **Open Worktree** on that row first.
2. In the Commit Panel, click **Compose commits with AI**.
3. Review the proposed commits. Reorder them, squash related ones together, or edit the messages.
4. Click **Create Commits** to apply them. If you want to start over, click **Reset** to go back to the proposal as it was before your edits. To leave without changing anything, click **Cancel**.

Compose commits from the agent's uncommitted changes.

***

## How to recompose commits the agent already made

Use this when the agent committed everything at once, or in many small steps that do not tell a clear story.

1. In the Commit Graph, hold Shift and click the agent's first and last commits to select the range.
2. Right-click the selection and select **Recompose *[number]* commits with AI (Preview)**, or click **Recompose commits with AI** in the Commit Panel.
3. Review the proposed structure. Reorder, squash, or edit messages until each commit does one thing and its message says what and why.
4. Click **Create Commits**. You can also click **Reset** to start over from the original proposal, or **Cancel** to leave without changing anything.

Recompose a range of the agent's commits.

Adjust the proposed commits before you apply them.

Recomposing keeps the original commit authors and adds co-authors when a new commit combines work from several people.

***

## How to check the new commits

Commit Composer does not change any code, so the final state of your branch is the same before and after. What changes is how the work is split up and described. Check that part before you share it:

1. **Read each new commit.** Click each commit and read its diff and message. A reviewer should be able to follow the change one commit at a time.
2. **Test each commit if your team needs every commit to build.** The newest commit has the same code as before, so this check is about the commits in between. Right-click each new commit, select **Checkout this commit**, and run your tests from the [embedded terminal](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/). Check out the agent's branch again when you're done. Your CI may also run this check for you.

If you do not like the result, click **Undo** in the toolbar right away. Undo reverses a Compose or Recompose action as long as you have not pushed the branch. The Undo tooltip lists the action as a rebase, because that is how GitKraken Desktop applies the new commits.

Click Undo to reverse a commit composition. The tooltip lists it as a rebase.

***

## How to share the cleaned-up branch

- **If you never pushed the branch,** push it as usual and [open a pull request](/gitkraken-desktop/pull-requests/).
- **If you already pushed it,** recomposing rewrote commits that are on the remote, so a normal push is rejected. GitKraken Desktop tells you the branch is behind the remote and offers **Pull**, **Force Push**, and **Cancel**. Select **Force Push**, then confirm. GitKraken Desktop uses a safe force push (force-with-lease), which stops if someone pushed to the branch since your last fetch. Use it only if nobody else has pulled or built on the branch. See [Push, Pull, and Fetch](/gitkraken-desktop/pushing-and-pulling/).

To write the pull request description, click the AI icon in the description field when you create the pull request to generate a draft, or right-click the branch and select **Explain Branch Changes** for a summary to start from. Edit either one so it says what you checked and what you did not.

***

## Common questions

Answers to frequent questions about cleaning up agent commits.

### Does Commit Composer change my code?

No. It only reorganizes the changes into new commits and rewrites their messages. The final code on your branch is the same before and after.

### Can I recompose commits from more than one agent session?

Not across a merge. Recompose only works on commits that are next to each other on the branch you have checked out, with no merge commits in the range. Clean up each agent's branch on its own first, then combine them. See [Resolve Merge Conflicts Between AI Agent Branches](/gitkraken-desktop/agent-merge-conflicts/).

### Can I clean up commits without AI?

Yes. Use [interactive rebase](/gitkraken-desktop/interactive-rebase/) to reorder, squash, and reword commits by hand.

### How do I see what the agent changed before I clean it up?

See [Review and Undo AI Coding Agent Changes](/gitkraken-desktop/review-and-undo-agent-changes/).

***

# Clean Up AI Coding Agent Worktrees and Branches in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/clean-up-agent-worktrees/
Description: See every worktree your coding agents left behind in one place in GitKraken Desktop, check which ones are merged, and remove or prune them safely.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Pull Request Filter Syntax
Content type: reference
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

GitKraken Desktop shows all of a repository's worktrees in one place, including the ones your coding agents created, and lets you remove them with or without their branches. Use this page to find stale agent worktrees and orphaned branches, check whether their work was merged, and clean them up without losing work you meant to keep.

**Requirements and limits**
- Scope: Finding, checking, and removing worktrees and branches left behind by coding agent sessions
- Prerequisite: The merged PR pill needs the branch's remote on GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket, or Bitbucket Data Center, with that integration connected.
- Limits: **Remove worktree and delete branch** deletes the local branch even if its commits are not merged, and you cannot undo it.
- Limits: You cannot remove the main worktree.

Removing a worktree also deletes its folder, including uncommitted and untracked files, once you confirm. Check the worktree before you remove it.

***

## Quick Start

Find the worktree in the Left Panel or in the Agents view, right-click it, and use the row that matches what you want to keep.

| What you want | Select | What it deletes |
|---|---|---|
| Keep the branch, remove the worktree | **Remove this worktree** | The worktree and its folder |
| Remove the worktree and its local branch | **Remove worktree and delete branch** | The worktree, its folder, and the local branch, merged or not |
| Remove everything, including the pushed branch | **Remove worktree and delete branch (local & remote)** | The worktree, its folder, the local branch, and the remote branch |
| Clear out worktrees whose folders are already gone | **Prune worktrees** | Git's records of worktrees that no longer exist on disk |
| Make sure a worktree is not removed by mistake | **Lock this worktree** | Nothing. Locked worktrees need extra confirmation to remove. |

***

## How to see all your worktrees in one place

Every worktree in the repository appears in three places:

- **List view in the Left Panel** lists each worktree with its branch. When the folder name differs from the branch, it appears under the branch name. Hover to see the full path.
- **The Agents view** shows a card for each worktree with its branch, uncommitted (WIP) changes, ahead and behind counts, and agent status.
- **The Commit Graph** shows a separate WIP row for each other worktree that has uncommitted changes or an active agent session, with the agent's status. Select a row and click **Open Worktree**, or double-click it, to open that worktree. To hide these rows, clear **Show worktree WIP nodes in the graph** in the **Agents** section of Repo-Specific Preferences.

The Agents view shows a card for every worktree.

***

## How to check a worktree before you remove it

A clean worktree does not tell you whether its work was merged. Check these first:

1. **Look for the merged PR pill.** A merged PR pill on the worktree's card means the branch has a merged pull request or merge request on GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket, or Bitbucket Data Center. The work has shipped, so it's safe to remove the worktree and delete the branch.
2. **Check the ahead count.** If the card shows the branch is ahead, it has commits that are not on the remote. Push them or make sure you do not need them.
3. **Check for WIP changes.** Uncommitted changes are deleted with the worktree. Open the worktree and commit, stash, or discard them first.
4. **Review the work if you're unsure.** See [Review and Undo AI Coding Agent Changes](/gitkraken-desktop/review-and-undo-agent-changes/).

***

## How to remove agent worktrees

Right-click the worktree in the Left Panel, or right-click its card in the Agents view, and choose one of the options below. Removing a worktree also stops any agent terminal session running in it.

Remove options on a worktree card in the Agents view.

### Remove the worktree and keep its branch

Select **Remove this worktree**. GitKraken Desktop removes the worktree and its folder. The branch and its commits stay, so you can check out the branch again later.

### Remove the worktree and its local branch

Select **Remove worktree and delete branch**, then confirm. GitKraken Desktop removes the worktree and then deletes the local branch.

It deletes the branch even if its commits are not merged anywhere, and you cannot undo it. Use it after the work is merged, or when you're sure you do not need the agent's commits. If the branch was pushed, the remote branch stays.

### Remove the worktree and the remote branch too

If the branch has a remote branch, the menu also shows **Remove worktree and delete branch (local & remote)**. It removes the worktree first, then deletes the local and remote branches. If the worktree is not removed, for example because you cancel, GitKraken Desktop deletes neither branch.

Only use this when nobody else needs the remote branch.

***

## What happens when a worktree has uncommitted changes

Git will not remove a worktree that has modified or untracked files, that is locked, or that contains submodules. In those cases, GitKraken Desktop asks whether to complete the removal with force. Select **Force Remove Worktree** to delete the worktree and everything in it, or **Cancel** to keep it.

Force removal cannot be undone. If you're not sure, cancel, open the worktree, and look at its WIP changes first.

***

## How to clean up worktrees whose folders are gone

If a worktree's folder was deleted outside GitKraken Desktop, for example by an agent or from your file manager, Git still keeps a record of it. The worktree still appears in the Left Panel, but you cannot open it.

To clean them up, right-click a prunable worktree in the Left Panel and select **Prune worktrees**. GitKraken Desktop runs `git worktree prune` for the repository, which clears every record whose folder no longer exists. Pruning does not delete any branches.

***

## How to protect a worktree from removal

Right-click the worktree and select **Lock this worktree**. Git will not remove a locked worktree without force, so GitKraken Desktop asks for confirmation before it does. To unlock it, select **Unlock this worktree**.

***

## Common questions

Answers to frequent questions about removing agent worktrees and branches.

### Will removing an agent's worktree delete its commits?

Not with **Remove this worktree**. The commits stay on the branch. **Remove worktree and delete branch** deletes the branch, and any commits that exist only on that branch are lost.

### Can I undo removing a worktree?

No. GitKraken Desktop warns that removing a worktree and deleting its branch cannot be undone. Check the worktree first, as described in [How to check a worktree before you remove it](#how-to-check-a-worktree-before-you-remove-it).

### Does GitKraken Desktop delete a branch that isn't merged?

Yes, if you select **Remove worktree and delete branch** and confirm. It does not check whether the branch is merged. Use the merged PR pill or the ahead count to check first.

### How do I know which worktrees an agent created?

Worktrees from agent sessions appear as cards in the Agents view, with the agent's status. Every worktree also appears in List view, whether an agent or a person created it.

***

## Related pages

- [Manage Git Worktrees](/gitkraken-desktop/worktrees/)
- [Coding Agents in GitKraken Desktop](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/)
- [Review and Undo AI Coding Agent Changes](/gitkraken-desktop/review-and-undo-agent-changes/)
- [Pull Requests](/gitkraken-desktop/pull-requests/)

# Review and Undo AI Coding Agent Changes in GitKraken Desktop
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/review-and-undo-agent-changes/
Description: See exactly what an AI coding agent changed in your Git repository and safely undo it in GitKraken Desktop with discard, reset, or revert.
Product: GitKraken Desktop
Feature: Pull Request Filter Syntax
Content type: reference
Audience: developer
Plan required: all
Status: GA
Last verified: 2026-03

Use this page to see exactly what an AI coding agent changed in your repository and to undo those changes safely if something went wrong. It works with any agent that edits files in a Git repository. GitKraken Desktop reads the changes from Git, so it does not matter which agent made them.

**Requirements and limits**
- Scope: Reviewing and reversing an agent's changes, whether they are uncommitted, committed on your machine, or pushed
- Prerequisite: The repository the agent worked in is open in GitKraken Desktop. The steps work for sessions started from the Agents view and for agents you run yourself.
- Limits: Git does not record whether a person or an agent wrote a change, so give each agent its own session or branch.
- Limits: AI summaries require a [paid GitKraken subscription](https://www.gitkraken.com/pricing?source=help_center&product=gitkraken). Reviewing diffs and undoing changes do not.

Discarding changes and hard resets remove work from the worktree you have open, including uncommitted changes that are not the agent's. Review the diff first.

***

## Quick Start

Before you undo anything, open the agent's worktree: in the Agents view, right-click the session card and select **Open this worktree**. Discard, restore, reset, and revert all act on the worktree you have open.

Then find where the agent's changes are and use the matching row.

| Where the changes are | How to see them | How to undo them | Safe after you push? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uncommitted, in the agent's worktree | Open the agent's worktree, click its WIP node, then click a file | Discard all or selected files, or revert one hunk | Not applicable | Discarded changes leave the worktree |
| Committed on the agent's branch, not pushed | Shift + click the agent's first and last commits for a combined diff of the range | Reset the branch to the last good commit | No | Reset rewrites the branch's history |
| Committed and pushed | Select the agent's commits in the Commit Graph | **Revert commit** on each one, then push | Yes | Revert adds new commits and keeps existing history |
| Only one or two files are damaged | Open the file's **History** | **Restore file from this commit** | Yes | The restored file arrives as a staged change |
| Anywhere in a session you do not want | Check the session card in the Agents view | **Remove worktree and delete branch** | No | Deletes the branch even if its commits are not merged |

***

## Before the agent starts: give it its own branch

Isolated changes are the easiest to review. When you start a session from the [Agents view](/gitkraken-desktop/agents/), GitKraken Desktop creates a new branch in its own [worktree](/gitkraken-desktop/worktrees/), so the agent's work stays separate from yours.

If you run an agent outside the Agents view, create a branch or worktree for it first. Then everything on that branch is the agent's work, and undoing it never touches your own changes.

***

## How to see what an agent changed

Where you look depends on whether the agent committed its work.

### See uncommitted changes

GitKraken Desktop shows a separate WIP row in the Commit Graph for each other worktree that has uncommitted changes or an active agent session. Rows for agent sessions show the agent's logo and current status. To hide these rows, clear **Show worktree WIP nodes in the graph** in the **Agents** section of Repo-Specific Preferences.

Each worktree, including each agent session, gets its own WIP node.

Selecting another worktree's WIP row does not open its files in the Commit Panel. Open the worktree first:

1. In the Agents view, check the session card for the branch, WIP changes, and ahead and behind counts.
2. Open the agent's worktree. Select its WIP row in the Commit Graph and click **Open Worktree**, or double-click the row.
3. Click the WIP node of the worktree you now have open. The Commit Panel lists every file the agent changed.
4. Click a file to open its [diff](/gitkraken-desktop/diff/). Use **Hunk** view to step through each changed block, or **Split** view to see the old and new versions side by side.

### See commits the agent made

1. Click a commit on the agent's branch, then click any file in the Commit Panel to see what that commit changed.
2. To see everything the agent committed at once, hold Shift and click the first and last of its commits. The Commit Panel shows **Viewing diff of *[number]* commits**, the list of selected commits, and the files changed across them. If the range ends at the commit you have checked out, you can include the WIP node too.

To compare 2 specific commits, hold Cmd (Mac) or Ctrl (Windows/Linux) and click each one. A combined diff of 3 or more items needs a contiguous range. For any other selection, the Commit Panel explains that a combined diff is not shown.

Select a range of commits to review an agent's work as one combined diff.

To compare the agent's uncommitted work with another branch, open the agent's worktree. Then right-click `main`, or whichever branch you want to compare against, in the Commit Graph and select **Compare commit against working directory**.

### Trace a single line

Open a file's diff and click **Blame** to see which commit last changed each line, or **History** to see every commit that touched the file. Blame and History help when an agent changed a file several times during one session.

### Get a summary with GitKraken AI

Right-click the agent's branch and select **Explain Branch Changes** to get a plain-language summary of everything on the branch. To explain specific commits, select 1 or 2 commits or a contiguous range. In the top-right corner of the Commit Panel, click **Explain commit** or **Explain commits**. If the AI button shows a **Recompose** label instead, open its menu and select the **Explain** option.

A summary helps you decide where to look first, but it is not a review. Read the diff before you keep or undo anything. See [GitKraken AI](/gitkraken-desktop/gkd-gitkraken-ai/) for details.

***

## How to undo an agent's changes

Pick the method based on where the changes are. Committed changes need more care to undo than uncommitted ones, and pushed changes need the most.

### Undo uncommitted changes

To throw away everything the agent changed but did not commit:

1. Open the agent's worktree.
2. Select the agent's WIP node.
3. Click the trash icon to discard all changes, or select specific files, right-click, and select **Discard *[number]* files**.

To keep most of the agent's work and undo one block, open the file's diff in **Hunk** view and click **Revert Hunk** next to that hunk. GitKraken Desktop applies the opposite change to your working directory. Reverting a hunk changes uncommitted files only. It's different from **Revert commit**, which adds a new commit that reverses an earlier one.

Revert a single hunk and keep the rest of the agent's changes.

See [Stage, Unstage, and Ignore Files](/gitkraken-desktop/staging/) for line-level options.

### Bring back an earlier version of a file

If the agent damaged one or two files, restore them instead of undoing everything:

1. Open the agent's worktree.
2. Open the file's diff and click **History**. Find the last commit that changed the file before the agent started.
3. Select that commit in the Commit Graph.
4. In the Commit Panel, right-click the file and select **Restore file from this commit**.

The file arrives in your working directory as a staged change, ready to commit. If you already have uncommitted changes to that file, GitKraken Desktop asks before it overwrites them.

### Undo commits that are only on your machine

If the agent committed work you have not pushed, reset its branch to the last good commit:

1. Open the agent's worktree.
2. Right-click the last commit you want to keep.
3. Select **Reset *[branch]* to this commit**, then choose a reset type:
   - **Soft** keeps the agent's changes staged, so you can review them and recommit only what you want.
   - **Mixed** keeps the changes in your working directory, unstaged.
   - **Hard** removes the agent's commits and every uncommitted change in the worktree.

Hard also deletes uncommitted changes in that worktree that the agent did not make. If you might want to keep any part of the work, start with Soft or Mixed.

See [How to reset commits](/gitkraken-desktop/commits/#resetting-commits) for more on reset types.

### Undo commits you already pushed

Once the agent's commits are on a shared branch, do not reset. Reverse them with new commits instead, so nobody else's history changes:

1. Open the agent's worktree.
2. Right-click the agent's newest commit in the Commit Graph and select **Revert commit**. GitKraken Desktop creates a new commit that undoes it.
3. Repeat for each commit you want to reverse, from newest to oldest.
4. Push the branch to share the revert commits.

Revert creates a new commit, so shared history stays intact.

### Throw away a whole agent session

If you do not want any of the session's work, right-click the session card in the Agents view and select **Remove worktree and delete branch**, then confirm. GitKraken Desktop stops the agent's terminal session and deletes the worktree, its working directory, and the local branch. It deletes the branch even if its commits are not merged anywhere, and you cannot undo this.

If the worktree still has uncommitted changes, GitKraken Desktop asks you to confirm again with **Force Remove Worktree**. The remote branch stays unless you choose **Remove worktree and delete branch (local & remote)** instead. If other people use the pushed branch, revert its commits instead of deleting it.

See [Clean Up AI Coding Agent Worktrees and Branches](/gitkraken-desktop/clean-up-agent-worktrees/) for more on removing worktrees.

***

## How to recover from a cleanup mistake

If you discard or reset the wrong thing while cleaning up after an agent, click **Undo** in the toolbar or press Cmd + Z (Mac) or Ctrl + Z (Windows/Linux) right away. Undo reverses the most recent supported action, such as a commit, a discard, or a branch reset, as long as it happened on your machine and has not been pushed. That includes commits and resets an agent made from its terminal, as long as you have the agent's worktree open. Undo is not available while a merge or rebase is in progress.

Undo reverses one action at a time, starting with the most recent. To reverse a series of agent commits, or commits you already pushed, use reset or revert, as in [Undo commits that are only on your machine](#undo-commits-that-are-only-on-your-machine) and [Undo commits you already pushed](#undo-commits-you-already-pushed). See [Undo and Redo](/gitkraken-desktop/undo-and-redo/) for the full list of supported actions.

***

## Common questions

Answers to frequent questions about reviewing and undoing agent changes.

### Can GitKraken Desktop tell which changes an agent made?

No. Git does not record whether a person or an agent wrote a change. GitKraken Desktop shows changes by branch and worktree, so when each agent works in its own session, its branch and WIP node show only that agent's work.

### Which agents does this work with?

Any agent that edits files in a Git repository. The Agents view integrates with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, and you can run other agents in the [embedded terminal](/gitkraken-desktop/terminal/). You review and undo changes from all of them the same way.

### Should I use a hard reset to undo an agent?

Only for commits that exist on your machine alone, and only after you've reviewed the diff. A hard reset also deletes every uncommitted change in the worktree. For anything already pushed, use **Revert commit**.

### Can I keep some of the agent's work and undo the rest?

Yes. Revert individual hunks, restore individual files, or use a **Soft** reset to put the agent's changes back in staging so you can commit only the parts you want.
